question: Should external Feishu verification-token callbacks remain supported as provider-native authentication, while truly unauthenticated public modes such as the current Matrix webhook are intentionally made fail-closed on upgrade?
rationale: The branch combines a necessary security boundary with a stronger-than-provider-native Feishu policy and construction-time compatibility breaks; only maintainers can confirm which breakages are intentional product policy.

options.title: Honor native auth and fail closed
options.body: Treat Feishu verification tokens as authenticated, keep genuinely unauthenticated external ingress disabled, and add clear upgrade diagnostics for affected configurations.

options.title: Require encrypted Feishu callbacks
options.body: Intentionally require Feishu encryption externally and document this as a Crabline security policy that is stricter than the provider contract.

options.title: Add an explicit strict mode
options.body: Preserve current external behavior by default and make construction-time fail-closed enforcement an opt-in configuration policy.

recommendation.title: Honor native auth and fail closed
recommendation.body: Treat Feishu verification tokens as authenticated, keep genuinely unauthenticated external ingress disabled, and add clear upgrade diagnostics for affected configurations.

likelyOwner.reason: This repository member currently owns the cross-provider security-boundary implementation and is best positioned to coordinate the intended policy with other maintainers.
